A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EMMA, with matching authors, architecture, and retained experiments. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2 support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, hallucination tests, visual-representation analyses, and a text-encoder ablation in Sections 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds relationship-hallucination evaluations and a controlled adapter-architecture ablation.

M1.justification: The primary EMMA pipeline remains unchanged. However, v2 introduces an experimental EMMA cross-attention variant replacing the linear Visual Alignment layer for the ablation in Table 4. This is a limited architectural adaptation, rather than a replacement of the proposed linear model.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 5a extends hallucination evaluation to MMRel-DallE, MMRel-VG, and R-Bench image-level and instance-level settings. The existing academic, instruction-following, AMBER, and FOIL coverage is retained. Newly named training sources document the previously described training mixture rather than establish a changed mixture.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds QA-ViT, reporting 80.5 on VQAv2 and 36.5 on VizWiz. Table 4 also introduces EMMA Cross-Attention as a comparator to linear EMMA and LLaVA-1.5. Existing benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled architecture comparison using the same stated training setup and 1.2M samples for LLaVA, linear EMMA, and cross-attention EMMA. Existing pretraining and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged. Table 1 also revises the reported BLIP-2/InstructBLIP vision-encoder size from 1B to 1.3B, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new eight-benchmark linear-versus-cross-attention ablation directly tests whether EMMA benefits from its simple alignment architecture, substantially strengthening the analysis of a central design choice. Hallucination robustness tests also expand to MMRel and R-Bench. Existing text-layer, mutual-information, and MMVP-distance analyses remain, while the token-weight L2 histogram and one MMVP example are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or uncertainty across training runs. The empirical histograms do not introduce such uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new comparison results appear. v2 Table 4 reports cross-attention versus linear EMMA scores of 8.67 versus 34.00 on MMVP and 29.50 versus 29.08 on MuirBench. Figure 5a adds results including MMRel-VG accuracy of 59.4 for LLaVA and 69.3 for EMMA. QA-ViT results are also added; rounded AMBER/FOIL redisplays do not establish changed performance.

T1.justification: v2 adds encoder and projection notation and Equation 1 for the already described alignment pipeline. v1 already defines the alignment map and weight matrix. These additions restate the existing procedure rather than introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: lightweight instruction-aware visual alignment, improvements up to 9.3%, stronger hallucination robustness, and competitiveness against larger models. New experiments support these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the cross-attention variant's weaker results as potential overfitting and argues that adapter complexity must be balanced against training-set size, particularly with 1.2M samples. This adds a substantive qualification to the simplicity argument; the earlier alignment and text-layer interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 names LVIS-Instruct4V, CLEVR, VizWiz, and ScienceQA within the previously unspecified 1.2M fine-tuning mixture. Tables 2–3 add vision-encoder identities and detail BRAVE's encoder collection. Conversely, v1's code-access statement and repository link disappear; the PDFs do not establish whether the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds a short discussion of Question-Aware Vision Transformers and their claimed generality tradeoff, plus references for the new robustness benchmarks, disclosed training sources, and BRAVE's encoders. The broader positioning against mPLUG-Owl2 and BRAVE remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 clarifies the pipeline description, reorganizes the analysis subsections, moves training-stage explanations into Implementation Details, and adds publication information. These are localized revisions rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figures undergo extensive regrouping: token analyses, mutual information and performance, and MMVP examples and distances become paired displays. The hallucination table becomes an expanded bar chart paired with the text-layer radar plot. Benchmark tables gain vision-encoder columns, a new ablation table appears, and the document adopts the TMLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2's controlled adapter ablation provides more direct evidence for the linear design, while added hallucination tests and training-mixture disclosure strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed code link, but remain limited by sparse implementation details for the new experiments and an overfitting explanation that is not directly tested.
